title: Daily routine
description: Say what you do every day.

explanation.summary: Most Spanish verbs end in -ar, and they all work the same way. Learn the pattern once and you can conjugate every verb in this unit without another word.

sections.heading: The six endings
sections.body: Take the infinitive, drop the -ar, and add the ending: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. Hablar becomes hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. The accent on habláis is what keeps it different from hablo, so do not drop it.

sections.heading: Tú and usted
sections.body: You take the tú form for people you know well, and the usted form for anyone you should be polite to. The usted form adds an r to the yo form: hablo becomes hable, hablas becomes hable. Talking to a friend you use hablas; talking to a stranger you use hable.

sections.heading: What happens every day
sections.body: To say how often, the adverb goes after the verb: siempre, todos los días, a veces. With a time you use a: trabajo por la mañana. The word for every day is todos los días, and it is plural even though it means one day.

examples.en: I always have coffee for breakfast.
